# onpager_team_responder_guard_policy (Resource)

Manage one team's explicit responder guard policy override. Create requires an unconfigured override; import existing policies before applying. Destroy resets the override to the current backend default and preserves historical publications.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_team_responder_guard_policy" "example" {
  team_id                       = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
  max_open_requests_per_subject = 25
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `max_open_requests_per_subject` (Number) Explicit maximum pending responder requests for the initiator team per subject, across owners. Required integer from 1 through 1000, without a default or unlimited value. Omitted/null and unknown values at apply are invalid. Publishing requires an active team; setting a value equal to the current backend default still creates an explicit override.
- `team_id` (String) Immutable owning team UUID, required without a default. Null and empty strings are invalid. Changing it replaces the resource. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable policy identity and import ID: the owning team UUID.
- `revision` (Number) Positive observed publication revision for this explicit override. This counter is metadata, never an If-Match or other write precondition. Concurrent publications apply in backend commit order; updates and resets are not compare-and-swap operations.

## Import

Import an existing explicit override with its owning team UUID. Import and
refresh read only. An inherited backend default is not a managed override and
cannot be imported. Inactive owners with explicit policies remain readable.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_team_responder_guard_policy.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_team_responder_guard_policy.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
```

## Ownership and lifecycle

Manage at most one guard policy resource per team. It owns the team's complete
explicit `max_open_requests_per_subject` override, an integer from 1 through
1000. There is no unlimited value. The API applies this pending responder request
cap per subject for the initiator team, across owners. Publishing an explicit
value equal to the backend default still creates an owned override.

Create first reads the exact team policy. An existing explicit override requires
import, even when its limit matches configuration. The provider never silently
adopts an unowned policy. Publishing requires an active team. Updates publish a
new immutable revision and populate state directly from the complete receipt.
The observed revision is metadata; publications and resets have no compare-and-swap
precondition and do not send `If-Match`. Concurrent writes apply in backend
commit order. No responder request, call, notification or preview is created.

Destroy uses the API's direct reset operation. It restores the current backend
default and preserves publication history. The provider neither guesses a
default limit nor restores a previously observed value. Reset supports inactive
owners and repeated calls. Other team configuration remains independent.

Only a successful, complete read with `is_default = true` and `revision = 0`
confirms logical absence. Authentication, authorization, transport and malformed
response errors, including HTTP 404, retain state. Failed publications and resets
retain saved state and are not retried automatically. A malformed successful
publication receipt preserves the known desired team and limit, clears the
unverifiable computed revision and reports an error; refresh recovers observed
metadata.

## Permissions

Create, refresh and import require `responder_guard_policies.read` in the owning
team. Create publication, updates and destroy require
`responder_guard_policies.publish`. Service accounts are supported through
explicit native role assignments; issuing a token alone grants no access.
